definition: A weight-initialization scheme that keeps the variance of activations and gradients stable across layers.
details: Poor initialization lets signals vanish or explode as they pass through deep networks, stalling training. Xavier (Glorot) initialization scales weights according to the number of input and output units so that variance is preserved layer to layer; it was a key enabler for training deep feedforward and recurrent networks.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Here is the short version: A weight-initialization scheme that keeps the variance of activations and gradients stable across layers. The part that makes it sing: Poor initialization lets signals vanish or explode as they pass through deep networks, stalling training. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Xavier Initialization — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
